description: We are focused on solving real-world agricultural challenges for the NASA Hackathon. Our project centers on farm fields, leveraging AI integration, AI agents, and efficient backend logic to build a working, impactful prototype. By turning complex environmental and satellite data into actionable insights, we aim to build technology that directly supports farmers, optimizes resources, and improves sustainability.
summary:
AgroShift AI is an open-source, climate-smart crop succession and agronomic decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth Observations into actionable multi-year crop rotations. Traditional agricultural applications suffer from a critical limitation: they recommend only single, isolated crops based on basic soil chemistry. In reality, sustainable farming relies on multi-season crop successions to biologically recharge soil nitrogen, break pest and disease lifecycles, and protect depleting aquifers.

Developed for smallholders, extension officers, and regional planners, AgroShift AI integrates daily NASA POWER agroclimatological data (precipitation, 2-meter air temperature, and solar insolation) with a deterministic 13-crop agronomic knowledge matrix (FAO-56 and PARC verified). The platform introduces a signature What-If Climate Stress Simulator, enabling farmers to model climate shocks (-40% rainfall deficit, +4°C heat spikes, and canal water rationing) and visualize decadal yield impacts from the 2020s through the 2060s in real time. Backed by transparent mathematical scoring, parcel-level multi-field succession planners, and a grounded AI copilot, AgroShift AI equips agricultural communities with the intelligence needed to build climate-resilient farming futures.
details:
1. Purpose & Working:

AgroShift AI is a full-stack, cloud-native agro-ecological intelligence engine. When a farmer or extension officer selects their land parcel on an interactive OpenStreetMap canvas or chooses an agro-ecological preset, the platform pinpoints the exact geographic coordinates and queries the NASA POWER Agroclimatology dataset. It pulls daily precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), 2-meter air temperature (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), and surface downward solar irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN).

These observations are synthesized into derived agronomic indicators (heat stress blast days >= 35°C, consecutive dry-spell streaks, and seasonal crop water balances). The system evaluates candidate rotational sequences across our 13-Crop Universal Matrix using a transparent deterministic scoring formula:

Match Score = (Climate Suitability x 30%) + (Water Balance Index x 25%) + (Soil Physico-Chemical Fit x 25%) + (Farmer Operational Priority x 20%).

Farmers can manage multi-field parcels, customize future seasons (2026 -> 2027 -> 2028), and run parametric climate stress simulations to project decadal harvest yields and discover resilient rotation rankings.

2. Benefits:

- Multi-Season Crop Succession: Replaces short-sighted single-season advice with sustainable 3-year sequences that naturally break pest life cycles (e.g., pink bollworm in cotton, root-knot nematodes).

- Biological Soil Regeneration: Maximizes symbiotic legume nitrogen fixation (injecting 45 to 110 kg N/ha), reducing synthetic urea expenditures by 30-45%.

- Aquifer & Water Table Protection: Quantifies evapotranspiration vs canal/groundwater supply, steering arid zones toward C4 cereals and drought pulses (saving up to 55% irrigation water).

- Parametric Stress Foresight: Farmers visualize decadal yield trajectories under +4°C heatwaves and canal curtailment before investing seasonal capital.

3. Impact

AgroShift AI bridges the gap between petabytes of Earth observation data and smallholder farming reality. By making complex satellite climatology accessible in an intuitive, responsive interface, the project empowers climate-vulnerable agricultural communities across South Asia and developing agro-economies to build climate-resilient farming futures, prevent crop failures, stabilize rural food security, and conserve critical groundwater aquifers.

4. Tech Stack:

- Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Recharts (responsive multi-line climate and yield projection charts), and Leaflet OpenStreetMap.

- Backend & APIs: Next.js Serverless Edge API Routes, FastAPI / Python 3.11/3.14, Pydantic, and SQLite/In-Memory State Store.

- Satellite & Climatology Data: NASA POWER (Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources) REST API, FAO-56 Crop Evapotranspiration Guidelines, and PARC Agro-Ecological Data.

- AI Copilot: Groq LPU Inference Engine (Llama-3.3-70b-Versatile) grounded with NASA measurements and calculated engine metrics.

- Deployment & CI/CD: Vercel Edge Serverless Platform (100% zero-card serverless architecture) and Git/GitHub.

5. Creativity:

Rather than treating satellite data as static background graphs, AgroShift AI couples NASA Earth Observations directly to a live What-If Parametric Shock Simulator. Moving vertical stress sliders immediately recalculates decadal harvest curves, triggers future climate hazard alerts (pollen sterility risk, root-zone deficit, canal cut impact), and inverts crop rotation rankings in real time (e.g., dynamically demonstrating how drought-hardy Pearl Millet and Chickpea overtake water-intensive cereal monocultures as temperatures rise).

6. Factors:

- Algorithmic Transparency: Avoided unexplainable blackbox AI; every recommendation score displays its exact mathematical formula breakdown.

- Agronomic Grounding: Modeled soil texture porosity (Sandy vs Loamy vs Clay), soil pH phosphorus lockout (alkaline pH > 8.0), and irrigation regimes (canal-groundwater turns vs tubewell rationing).

- Universal Accessibility: Built as a responsive, fullscreen-optimized web app requiring zero high-end hardware, zero installations, and zero subscription fees.
